nom: St. Ives Acne Control Apricot Face Scrub

segments.sensitive: Reviewers with sensitive or acne-prone skin report the scrub can feel too rough and cause irritation if used daily, but used three to four times a week it leaves skin soft, bright, and with reduced redness and fewer bumps, with only mild tightness and no burning or tingling.

concerns.blemishes: Most reviewers using the scrub for acne-related concerns report visible improvement over time, including fewer bumps, cleared blackheads, and breakouts kept at bay with regular use, with one calling it the best scrub she has found for problem-prone skin. One reviewer dissents, saying she was still breaking out after a week and a half of use, though she felt it was having some effect.
concerns.redness: The one reviewer who addresses redness directly, who has sensitive skin and uses the scrub once a week, reports it reduced redness and smoothed away most bumps, with only mild tightness afterward and no burning or tingling.
concerns.dehydration: A couple of reviewers report the scrub does not dry out skin despite being an exfoliant: one with sensitive skin says it does not strip moisture, and another notes it removes dry patches and leaves a more even, glowing complexion.
concerns.aging: A couple of long-term users, having used the scrub for a decade or more, report avoiding crow's feet or being regularly told they look younger than their age; one is careful to note this could partly reflect good genetics rather than the product alone.
concerns.spots: The one reviewer who mentions skin tone reports the scrub helped even it out, alongside removing dry patches and dead skin buildup, for a glowing complexion.

aspects.libelle: Sweet scent with a cooling feel
Leaves skin feeling fresh and soft
Good value, especially bought in bulk
Works well on body, not just face

extraits.texte: Called company. Can't get. Surly customer service agents that I couldn't understand and had to keep asking to repeat themselves. I needed more information on if the ingredients have been changed. The smell of this product is stronger; I can't use fragrance. I've used the original product for years. I have a lot of allergies including skin allergies. I've put an image of the original product I've been using below. Are there added ingredients in this new product?

I love this apricot scrub but definitely don’t use every day, most especially not twice a day. It can be too rough on acne prone/sensitive skin so only use 3 times a week, 4 max. I prefer doing it Monday, Wednesday or Thursday, and Saturday, only in the mornings because it does make my skin really soft and bright when I use it only a few days a week. Definitely worth the price and the rating. I’m rating 5 stars overall though because using it twice a day, everyday was my own fault, and once I settled into a routine of it a few times a week, it worked perfectly. Got a set of 4 bottles for about $18, and I love them

Hey guys! I’m reviewing the St. Ives Acne control Abricot scrub! - Damn, that’s a mouth full. - I’ve been using this once a week, for about 3 weeks, and i can say i’ve seen some improvement. - I use this once a week, because i have sensitive skin... - it has a sweet,yet subtle smell, and feels cooling on the skin. It does make my skin feel a little tight after but it did not burn, nor tingle. - my skin has cleared up a little, primarily getting rid of redness. - but my favorite thing about it, is that it smoothed my skin, getting rid of most of the bumps, while simultaneously getting rid of dead skin cells. - It’s an oil-free salicylic acid acne medication (Anti-inflammatory used to treat acne, psoriasis, or warts!) It’s also Paraben free, (which can clogs pores) and dermatologist tested. it contains 2.0% salicylic acid, btw. It’s inactive ingredients include : Water (Aqua), Juglans Regia (Walnut) Shell Powder, Glycol Stearate SE, Glycerin, Sodium Lauryl Sulfoacetate, Zea Mays (Corn) Kernel Meal, Cocamidopropyl Betaine, Cetearyl Alcohol, Triethanolamine, Cetyl Alcohol, Glyceryl Stearate, PEG-100 Stearate, Prunus Armeniaca (Apricot) Fruit Extract, Cetyl Acetate, Ceteareth-20, Carbomer, Polysorbate 60, Acetylated Lanolin Alcohol, Fragrance (Parfum), PPG-2 Methyl Ether, Phenethyl Alcohol, Methylisothiazolinone, Titanium Dioxide (CI 77891). - It’s most definitely going to stay in my rotation!
Honestly, i do see it’s doing something but I’m still breaking out so I would say acne control... still great I guess. This is after using it for a week and a half.

extraits.titre: Gentle dirt and oil exfoliant that also does not dry out your skin
extraits.texte: Same scrub that kept Price Rogers Nelson looking so good (appears on his beauty stand in his post death house pictures...who knew?), and a staple in my beauty routine as well for well over a decade and my skin looks great with folks regularly thinking me younger than I am! The crushed almond shells impart just enough abrasion to get the job done without being harsh to sensitive skin. #Winner

I love St. Ives Acne Control Scrub! I started using it many years ago because a friend said if you use it daily you can prevent crow's feet wrinkles. Here I am, 30 years later and I still don't have crow's feet! Maybe I'm just blessed with good skin, but I don't think so. I think it's the scrub. I use it on my whole face and neck when I shower. I'm always careful to rub it in well at the corners of my eyes where crow's feet develop and over my lips. It leaves my skin exfoliated and feeling fresh and clean. I've been using it for so long now I probably should have bought stock in the company!
